Do not accept: first finger current; first finger force; index finger current; index finger force. MP3 1 mark: Maps the second finger to conventional current. Accept: second finger represents current; middle finger shows conventional current; second finger gives current direction; middle finger indicates current; second finger is current; second finger is conventional current. Do not accept: second finger field; second finger force; middle finger field; middle finger force. Allow any wording that conveys the idea, including common alternatives, correct hedged answers ('I think ...') and clearly intended spelling. Ignore extra correct detail. self_check.instructions: Attempt first. After revealing the rubric, check each idea separately. Tick met only when your answer clearly states that idea; tick not met when it is absent, and unsure when you cannot decide. Synonyms, clear approved misspellings, number words and equivalent units can count. A correct word inside a wrong statement is not enough. The automatic result is a suggestion, separate from your self-assessment. Marking is tolerant of wording: any listed alternative, synonym or keyword for an idea counts, hedges such as 'I think' are ignored, and clearly intended spellings are accepted. A correct word inside a negated or contradicted statement is not credited.

significant_figure_policy.note: A value equal to the expected value rounded to the student's own number of significant figures (at least 2) is accepted; extra trailing zeros are fine.

numeric_rule.answer_selection_policy: Working may be shown. The last quantity carrying an acceptable unit is the answer; a quantity introduced by 'not'/'no' is ignored; an earlier correct value followed by a different final value needs review.
numeric_rule.unit_case_policy: Exact case first; otherwise case-insensitive only when it resolves to a single multiplier (mJ and MJ stay distinct).
numeric_rule.tolerance_basis: Exact simple-arithmetic target plus small floating-point allowance; no percentage window.
